description: Held-out causal-grounding evaluation set v1, drafted 2026-11-01 before CA-04..06 were implemented and evaluated once against policy a0b4adeb…; kept unchanged as historical evidence.

unsafe.text: Group returns are the bottleneck behind long case spans.
Route incidents directly to the final group to get them closed earlier.
Incidents would be handled in less time if returns were prevented.
We anticipate a meaningful drop in span once returns are addressed.
Measure the time saved per incident after removing returns.
Fewer returns translate into a 40% smaller span.
Removing the second group visit is the most promising lever for faster closure.
Each group return costs roughly five extra days.
Resolution performance stands to gain substantially.
Returns are a waste of agent time; cutting them pays off.

safe.text: The p90 observed case span is longer for incidents with a repeated group visit.
The review would describe which routing patterns co-occur with longer spans; it does not establish that changing them would shorten spans.
Compare matched cohorts by product and impact to determine whether the span difference persists.
Share of incidents with a repeated group visit, reported monthly with sample sizes.
